Just by way of disclaimer, the Tax Foundation is not pro-tariff to be sure. And additionally, one other challenge with estimates of tariffs is we don't actually have a lot of experience as a country or as a globe even with tariffs of the scale and size that Trump has, for instance, just imposed on Canada and Mexico. And so we don't have good modeling of the impact it might have. And by that, I mean, when you impose a tax or a tariff, There are behavioral impacts. People switch away. And we have some good modeling for regular old taxes because we have a lot of experience with them and at the state level, local, federal level. But we don't have a lot of experience with how people will switch, how they will substitute, how they will change doing business in response to tariffs. So with all of those caveats, lots of asterisks around these numbers, the Tax Foundation estimates that the current tariffs on China, Canada, and Mexico will raise between $230 and $300 billion a year or $2.6 trillion over 10 years.
